subject_line: America Finally Agrees With Us on Protein
opening: Happy Sunday, and welcome to the week where mainstream America caught up to what we've known for years. There's a lot packed into this issue, from a stat that'll make you feel like a trendsetter to a cooking fat breakdown that'll change how you think about your skillet. Grab your coffee and let's get into it.

hero.title: 70% of Americans Now Prioritize Protein. We've Been Saying This.
hero.teaser: For years, people called us extreme. Now, based on new consumer research, protein has officially beaten 'fresh' as America's number one food criterion. The carnivore community didn't just see this coming. We've been living it for a long time. Chloe breaks down what this shift actually means, and why the most interesting part isn't the stat itself.

supporting.title: Rendered Fat vs Butter: The Cooking Fat Protocol
supporting.teaser: Marcus lays out exactly which fat belongs in your pan for each job, including a method to render tallow at home for what he calls almost nothing per ounce.

supporting.title: Carnivore and Alcohol: What Happens When You Drink
supporting.teaser: Sarah explains the metabolic reason your two-drink limit now feels like four, and what to actually do about it before your next social event.

supporting.title: Meatstock 2026: What 1,600 Carnivores in One Room Looks Like
supporting.teaser: Chloe went to Meatstock, and the one thing she says you can't fake at a convention of 1,600 people might change how you think about this community.

try_this_week: Render your own tallow this week. Marcus walks through the full process in his cooking fat post, but the short version is: grab beef fat from your butcher, low oven heat, strain it, done. Community members who've tried it report the cost comes out to almost nothing per ounce, and the flavor difference in your next pan sear is immediately noticeable.
looking_ahead: Next week, we're getting into something Sarah has been quietly researching for months, and it has to do with why some long-term carnivores start feeling off after year two.
